get.summary: List devices for the organization context (X-Org).

parameters.name: integration_id
parameters.description: Optional filter: only devices belonging to this integration.

parameters.name: zone_id
parameters.description:
Optional filter: only devices placed directly in this zone. A malformed id is 400.
Combines with `q`; cannot be combined with `integration_id`.

parameters.name: device_kind
parameters.description:
Optional filter: only devices with metadata.kind equal to this value (e.g. virtual_access_portal).
Requires integration_id.

parameters.name: external_id
parameters.description:
Optional filter: only devices with this external_id. Requires integration_id and device_kind.
Returns at most 1 device.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Case-insensitive substring match on the device name in any locale. Best-effort when
`integration_id` is set.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Server-side ordering for org-wide lists: `name:asc`, `name:desc`, `created_at:asc`, `created_at:desc`.
Ignored when `integration_id` is set. Defaults to insertion order when omitted.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Locale used to resolve the localized `name` when sorting by name (e.g. `en`). Defaults to `en`.

parameters.name: has_external_id
parameters.description: When true, only devices with a non-empty `external_id`. Requires `integration_id`.

parameters.name: has_go2rtc_channel
parameters.description: When true, only devices whose metadata JSON has a non-empty `channel` (go2rtc cameras). Requires `integration_id`.

parameters.name: include_stale
parameters.description: When true with `integration_id`, include `stale` per device when the provider supports it.

parameters.name: org_scope
parameters.description:
`self` (default): org subtree of X-Org. `self_and_ancestors`: exact X-Org plus ancestor orgs
where the caller has `devices:list` (door-wiring camera pickers). Cannot combine with
`zone_id` or `integration_id`.

post.summary: Create an access invite granting portal_open on one or more portals.
post.description:
Safe for at-least-once delivery from an external system of record:

* `Idempotency-Key` makes a retried create replay the original result instead of creating a
  second invitation. The replayed body omits the one-time `invite_token` / `invite_url` and sets
  `idempotent_replay`.
* `external_ref` binds the invitation to a record in the calling system. A second create for the
  same record is rejected with `external_reference_conflict`; use the reconcile route to make an
  existing invitation match a desired state.
* `X-Correlation-Id` (or `X-Request-Id`) is stored with the invitation and on every audit event
  for the write, and echoed back on the response.

parameters.description: Replay key; a retry with the same key and body returns the original result without creating a second invitation.

post.summary: Make the invitation state for an external record equal a desired state.
post.description:
This is the operation a system of record needs: it addresses the invitation by
`external_ref`, so the caller never has to discover or store OpenApp invitation ids, and there is
no create-then-update race window. Behavior:

* `state: active`, no invitation for the record — creates one and returns the one-time token.
* `state: active`, invitation exists — updates it to the desired state (restoring it first when
  it was revoked, e.g. a reinstated reservation).
* `state: revoked` — revokes the invitation, or reports `unchanged` when it is already revoked or
  was never created. The guest link stops working; history and the external reference survive.

Out-of-order delivery is rejected: when `external_ref.revision` is older than the stored
revision the call fails with `external_revision_stale` and nothing is written. Duplicate
delivery is safe by construction, and `Idempotency-Key` additionally replays the original
response.

parameters.description: Replay key; a retry with the same key and body returns the original result.

put.description:
The update is a desired-state write and is therefore naturally idempotent: replaying the same
body leaves the same state. Out-of-order delivery is handled by `external_ref.revision` — a
write whose revision is older than the stored one is refused with `external_revision_stale`
instead of restoring an earlier room, window, or portal set.

post.summary: Revoke an access invite.
post.description:
Revocation is idempotent: revoking an already revoked invitation returns the same state with the
original `revoked_at`, so a duplicate checkout webhook is safe. It is also reversible through the
restore route, which is what makes a reinstated reservation recoverable; the invitation row,
its history, and its external reference are preserved (unlike delete).

post.summary: Import provider zones and placements into the integration's org.
post.description: Import the provider's zones (e.g. Home Assistant areas) into the integration's org and place its devices and entities. A provider zone already linked keeps its zone; an unlinked one links to the single org zone with the same normalized name, otherwise a zone is created (quota: `zones`, 1 per created zone). Devices take their provider zone; an entity whose provider zone differs from its device's is placed explicitly, otherwise it inherits. A placement a user changed since the last sync is never overwritten (`skipped_manual`). Requires `zones:create`, `devices:update`, and `entities:update` on the integration's org. Providers advertise support with `supports_zone_sync` in their definition.

post.summary: Redeem an invitation: exchange `token` + `pin` for org membership.
post.description:
Token and PIN are checked before the session. A wrong PIN yields 422 even when signed out,
so the redeem page can show feedback without sending the visitor to login. A correct PIN
with no session yields 401; the invitation stays pending. With a session, the invitation is
attached to that account unless its email or phone already belongs to someone else. Set
`merge_accounts` to start a combine-accounts offer instead of rejecting; the invitation
stays pending until that offer is confirmed. When the invitation names an email and the
signed-in mailbox is different, the caller must set `accept_on_signed_in_account`. That
keeps the membership on the current account and does not store the invited address. When
the account already has a different phone, `phone_action` chooses whether to keep that
number or replace it with the invited one.

AccessInviteContactInput.description:
One contact named by an invitation.

Exactly one of `email`, `phone`, `user_id`, and `group_id` is set, and it must match
`contact_kind`. Free-form contacts are normalized on write: a phone becomes E.164 using
`phone_region` when it is not already international.

phone.description: E.164, or national format when `phone_region` is supplied.

phone_region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region used to normalize a national-format phone.

AccessInviteContactNotification.description:
One notification attempt. `status` is `sent`, `failed`, or `bounced` — never `delivered`,
because no provider delivery receipt is ingested for any channel.

is_linked.description:
Whether the portal currently resolves to a live door device. When false the portal
is misconfigured/unlinked and the invite UI shows it in a warning state.

created_by_user_id.description: User who created this invite or share. Omitted when the row has no creator.

curfew_exempt.description: Admin-only emergency exception: skip invitation curfew at redemption.

oneOf.description: External system-of-record correlation, when this invitation is driven by an adapter.

Resolved event location for this invite (see `location_mode`): the invite's own
location when `explicit`, the building location when `inherit`, or absent when `none`.

location_mode.description: How the event location is resolved: `none`, `explicit`, or `inherit` (building).

photo_thumb_url.description:
Presigned URL for the `thumb` rendition of the invite photo, for avatar-sized renders.
Absent when the source is already thumb-sized; fall back to `photo_url`.

photo_url.description: Presigned URL for the invite's main photo (best-effort).

deleted_at.description: When set, the portal is soft-deleted (kept for restore).

device_id.description: Door device id (virtual_access_portal in this integration). Canonical portal link key.

directory_id.description: Directory device id (virtual_access_directory in this integration).

door_name.description: Localized door/action name (plain string or `{ locale: name }`). Set on invite-usage rows.

invite_name.description: Localized invitation name. Set on door-usage rows opened via an invitation.

date_of_birth.description: Parent-declared date of birth (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Required when `is_child` is true.

is_child.description: When true, this household member is a child; date of birth is required.

receives_calls.description: When omitted, defaults to false for minors and true for adults.

AddRolesRequest.description: Request type for adding/deleting roles (org_id -> list of role names).

admitted.description:
true admits the member, false denies them. A denial is durable, so it does not resurface
in the approval queue on every sync.

AdmissionResponse.description: One row of the admission ledger, including members who were removed.

AgeClass.description: Derived age class for call/portal limits. Not a marketing segment.

ApiErrorResponse.description: A minimal, user-facing error body for public API responses.

correlationId.description:
Server-generated correlation id that ties this error to the request trace and the
matching audit event (see the audit log). Present when the request carried one.

current_phone.description: Present when `error_code` is `invite_phone_choice`: the number already on the signed-in account.

error_code.description: Optional stable code for clients to branch on (e.g. "door_unreachable").

invited_phone.description: Present when `error_code` is `invite_phone_choice`: the number named by the invitation.

ApiKeyListItem.description: Response for API key list item (no token).

subject_kind.description: What the request is about, e.g. `invite`.

subject_label.description: Human-readable subject (invite name), not the raw kind/ref.

subject_ref.description: Id of the subject (e.g. the disabled invite link awaiting approval).

count.description: Number of distinct organization-admin approve votes required.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next (older) page, or null when the last page was returned.

download_url.description: Signed download URL, present only when `status = completed`.

zone_id.description: Zone filter the job was created with.

AuditOutcome.description:
Outcome of an audited action. `denied` (permission/quota refusal) is recorded too —
it is critical for security investigations.

AuditRecord.description:
A persisted audit event. Serialized shape doubles as the webhook payload and the pull-API
response item.

actor_guest_id.description:
Stable, client-supplied per-device guest fingerprint (ULID). Deliberately kept in its own
field, NEVER `actor_user_id`: a guest id is spoofable and must never be readable as a
trusted (registered) user identity, nor collide with the user-id population.

id.description: ULID; also the webhook idempotency key.

BillingAccount.description:
The billable entity for purchases. By default each member has a personal account; grouping
multiple users into one account lets one user be billed to another's account.

CapacityResource.description:
A capacity-tracked resource type that participates in the lifecycle. (Org members are
intentionally excluded — they are never auto-deleted.)

audience.description: Whether anyone holding the link may use the invitation, or only the named contacts.

contacts.description:
Who the invitation is for. Each contact is either free-form (an email address or a phone
number) or drawn from the organization (a person or a group). Rejected for shares, which
carry no invitee identity. Empty when the link is open to anyone.

creation_justification.description: Why this invitation is being created (required when `invitation_require_justification` applies).

curfew_exempt.description: Admin-only emergency exception: skip invitation curfew at redemption.

oneOf.description:
Correlation to the record in the external system of record that owns this invitation
(PMS reservation, work order, enrolment). One live invitation may own a given
`(source, record_id)` pair per integration, which is what makes retries and duplicate
webhook deliveries safe. Omit for invitations authored inside OpenApp.

has_photo.description: True when the client will upload a photo immediately after create (media is a follow-up POST).

location_id.description:
Reusable org-scoped location id to bind, only consumed when `location_mode` is `explicit`.
Create the location first via the locations API (which can geocode it), then reference it here.

oneOf.description:
How the event location is resolved. Defaults to `inherit` (use the building location) when
omitted. `explicit` binds to the reusable org location referenced by `location_id`; `none`
shows no event location.

max_devices.description: Virtual keycard limit: max unique devices allowed to redeem/use this invite. JSON `null` or omitted means unlimited.

max_uses.description: Omit to apply the share default (or leave invitations unlimited). JSON `null` means unlimited.

pin.description:
Host-chosen PIN (stored hashed). Required when `invitation_require_identity.require_pin`.
JSON `null` means no PIN; omission leaves the create default unchanged.

portal_ids.description: Portal ULIDs to grant. Array order is the display order on the public invite page.

schedules.description:
One or more validity windows. A single non-recurring entry is the ordinary case; a share is
exactly one entry with no explicit start (it opens at request time).

curfew_exempt.description: Admin-only emergency exception: skip invitation curfew at redemption.

curfew_windows.description: Effective forbidden hour windows (informational; invites are never mutated).

oneOf.description: External system-of-record correlation stored with the invitation.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this body is a replay of an earlier create that carried the same
`Idempotency-Key`. Nothing was created by this request and the one-time token fields are
omitted.

invite_token.description:
Guest bearer token, returned **once** by the original create call.

It is stored only as a hash, never logged, and never cached for idempotent replay, so a
replayed create response omits it. Persist it at delivery time or rotate it through
`POST /access-invites/{id}/regenerate-token`.

invite_url.description:
Guest-facing invite URL (shareable link for SMS/email). Same one-time visibility as
`invite_token`, and subject to the same logging restrictions.

oneOf.description: Resolved event location for this invite (see `location_mode`).

location_mode.description: How the event location is resolved: `none`, `explicit`, or `inherit` (building).

pending_approval.description:
True when a `user_sharing` policy required admin approval: the invite was created disabled
and an approval request is pending. The invite activates once an admin approves it.

timezone.description: Org IANA timezone used to evaluate invitation curfews.

device_id.description: Door device id (virtual_access_portal device in this integration). Links the portal to a door.

directory_id.description: Directory device id (virtual_access_directory in this integration).

name.description: Portal display name (localized). Accepts string or object e.g. { "en": "Lobby", "he": "לובי" }.

group_roles.description:
Group roles to add to the credential's default roles: any of `groups:create`,
`groups:read`, `groups:update`, `groups:delete`, `groups:list`, `groups:share`,
`groups:link`. Refused (403) unless the agent's organization has an enforcing
`agent_group_write` policy and the caller holds each role there. The credential can use
them only in the agent's organization, and only while that policy stays enforced.

expires_at.description: [RFC 3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339) absolute expiration timestamp (UTC). Mutually exclusive with `expires_in`.

expires_in.description: Duration per [RFC 5545 §3.3.6](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545#section-3.3.6) (ISO 8601 `P1D`, `PT1H`, …; no months/years) or compact tokens `s`/`m`/`h`/`d`/`w` (`M` is minutes). Max 3650d (10 years). `1y` is rejected. Mutually exclusive with `expires_at`.

scoped_entity_ids.description:
Limit the key to these entities (doors, lights). A key limited to entities cannot list,
create, or reach devices.

scoped_roles.description:
Limit the key to these roles. Omitted: the key acts with all of its owner's roles. Each
role must be one the owner holds in the org. Grantable roles: `entities:read`,
`entities:list`, `entities:create`, `entities:update`, `entities:delete`,
`entities:set_state`, `entities:set_hold`, `devices:read`, `devices:list`,
`devices:create`, `devices:update`, `devices:delete`, `integrations:read`,
`integrations:list`, `integrations:users:list`, `integrations:users:write`, `orgs:read`,
`orgs:list`, `users:read`, `users:list`, `users:create` (invite people to the org),
`zones:read`, `zones:list`, `zones:create`, `zones:update`, `zones:delete`. Group roles
are not grantable to API keys; manage groups with an unscoped key.

CreateApiKeyResponse.description: Response for API key creation (token shown once).

occurred_after.description: RFC 3339 lower bound (inclusive). Defaults to the start of retention.

occurred_before.description: RFC 3339 upper bound (inclusive). Defaults to now.

zone_id.description:
Zone ULID: export only events whose zone snapshot (`details.zone_path`) contains it
(the zone and its descendants). 400 when not a ULID.
Zone the device is placed in (same org). Entities with `zone.mode = inherit` take it.

metadata.description:
Arbitrary, persisted entity metadata (integration-specific).

For example, MQTT entities can store:
- `command_topic`
- `toggle_payload`

Values are stored as strings: non-string values are JSON-stringified.

name.description: Optional friendly name for the entity.

zone.description: Zone placement; defaults to `{"mode":"inherit"}` (follow the device zone).

expires_in_hours.description: Hours until the offer expires. Bounded so an offer cannot outlive the reason for it.

invitee_name.description:
Optional name for the person you invite. It greets them in the invitation and labels the
pending invitation for you. When they sign up without a name it becomes their account name,
and they are asked to confirm it. Blank counts as no name; at most 100 characters.

locale.description:
Language of the invitation SMS/email: a supported locale code. Used when the
contact has no account with a language of its own; resends reuse it. Omit to fall back to
the household's home org default message language, then English.

sms_consent_confirmed.description:
Must be `true` when `phone` is set: confirms the person you invite agreed to receive text
messages from OpenApp at that number. The confirmation is recorded with who gave it and
when. Not needed for email-only invitations.

name.description: Household name. Omit it to use the default derived from the caller.

oneOf.description:
Human-friendly name for this integration (optional; defaults server-side).
Accepts string or LocalizedString map, e.g. { "en": "Name", "he": "שם" }.

non_admin_acknowledgment.description: Required when `linked_account_admin` is `warn_and_ack` and the PalGate probe is non-admin.

date_of_birth.description:
Parent-declared date of birth (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Must classify as under 16. Applied to the
account at redeem when the account has none. Omit when the invitee is an adult.

default_group_ids.description: Groups the person joins when they redeem, in the same transaction as the org role.

default_roles.description: Roles to assign on accept (within the inviting org).

invitee_name.description:
Name of the person being invited, up to 100 characters. Greets them in the invitation
and labels the pending invitation for the inviter. At sign-up it becomes the account
name only when no name is known, and the person confirms it. Omit when unknown.

locale.description:
Language of the invitation SMS/email: a supported locale code. Used when the
contact has no account with a language of its own; resends reuse it. Omit to fall back to
the org's default message language, then English.

oneOf.description: Optional site (and listing) access applied atomically when the invitation is redeemed.

sms_consent_confirmed.description:
Must be `true` when `phone` is set: confirms the person being invited agreed to receive
text messages from OpenApp at that number. The confirmation is recorded with who gave it
and when. Not needed for email-only invitations.

redeem_url.description:
Shareable redeem URL — surfaced once so the inviter can hand it off out-of-band
(the PIN is never returned here).

locale.description:
Preferred locale (app code or BCP-47) for geocoding: controls the language of geocoded
text and the locale key it is tagged under. Defaults to `en` when omitted.

provider_place_id.description:
Opaque place id issued by `geocoding_provider`. Both fields must be sent together: a place id
cannot be resolved without naming its issuer.

signing_secret.description:
HMAC-SHA256 signing key, returned exactly once. The PMS signs each delivery with it (see
`POST /pms/{connector_id}/inbound`); it is never returned again.

config.description:
Typed-per-`policy_type` configuration document. For the documented typed
shapes, see `RequireStepUpPolicyConfig` and `ApprovalThresholdPolicyConfig`.

enforcement.description:
`enforce` (default) or `require_approval`. Each `policy_type` declares which modes it
accepts (only `user_sharing` accepts `require_approval`); any other value is rejected
with 400.

email.description: Login email. Omit for phone-only accounts.

first_name.description: Given name stored on the Kratos identity (`traits.name.first`) when creating the account.

last_name.description: Family name stored on the Kratos identity (`traits.name.last`) when creating the account.

phone.description: E.164 phone (`+[country][digits]`). When set, must satisfy the same pattern as Kratos.

roles.description: Org ID (string) to list of role names. Optional.

event_types.description: Event-type filter; omit or empty for all events.

signing_secret.description:
The HMAC signing secret, returned exactly once at creation. Store it securely; it is used to
verify the `X-OpenApp-Signature` header on every delivery and is never returned again.

oneOf.description:
Required for `wpa_psk` (password) and `wpa_enterprise` (username and password); rejected
for `open`.

priority.description: Lower values are listed first in text messages. Defaults to 0.

zone_ids.description: Zones the network covers. Each must be a live zone of the `X-Org` organization.

site_ids.description:
Access sites this zone belongs to. When omitted: inherit the parent's memberships if a
parent is set, otherwise unbound (empty).

end.description: Local clock `HH:MM`. Inclusive; may be earlier than `start` (midnight wrap).

DegradationStage.description: Lifecycle position of an org's over-capacity remediation.

DegradationStatus.description: Full over-capacity degradation snapshot for an org.

DeleteRolesRequest.description: Request type for deleting roles (org_id -> list of role names).

device_metadata.description:
Device-specific JSON metadata; its shape depends on the integration provider. Absent when
the device has none.

external_id.description: External ID from the integration provider.

zone_id.description: Zone the device is placed in (same org). Entities with `zone.mode = inherit` take it.

Device.description: A physical or virtual device belonging to an org and integration.

DeviceMetadataDefinitionResponse.description: Device metadata definition response (schema + current data) for schema-driven edit UI.

credentials_set.description: JSON Pointers into `data` of write-only credential fields that currently hold a value.

data.description: Current `device_metadata` as a JSON object, without write-only credential fields.

schema.description: JSON Schema describing the device's `device_metadata` for this provider.

credentials_set.description:
JSON Pointers into `device_metadata` of write-only credential fields (schema
`format: password`) that currently hold a value. Credential values are never returned
here; an update that omits them keeps the stored value and `null` clears it.

is_primary_instance.description:
Read-only, computed by the server: true when this device record is the primary instance
for its physical hardware, when the same hardware has more than one device record.
Never accepted in a request body.

stale.description: Present when `include_stale=true` was requested and the provider supports stale detection.

DeviceRuleResponse.description: One device-tier policy as it applies to one device of the integration.

output.description: Output the rule is scoped to, or null when it binds every output of the device.

DirectoryFloorListResponse.description: Distinct directory floors for a directory device.

DirectoryFloorSummary.description: One distinct floor among the listings of a directory device.

oneOf.description: Derived age class. Only set for listing managers.

date_of_birth.description: Calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`. Only set for listing managers.

message_locale.description:
Shipped locale code (`en`, `he`, `pt_br`) of the language messages to this person are
written in: their own choice, the language last seen in their app, then the org default.

user_email.description: Mailbox the person can sign in with. Omitted when the account has only a placeholder email.

user_phone.description: Verified E.164 phone on the account, when one is set.

timezone.description: Organization IANA timezone used when authoring a new recurring hold.

EffectiveLimit.description: Resolved limit for a subject, quota key, and period, with the source that set it.

source.description:
Where this value came from: an override, the org's tier, the system default, or the
platform exemption.

value.description: The effective cap, in the quota's unit. Null means unlimited.

allowed_portal_ids.description: Present on integration effective-policies when listing-restrict binds this requester.

device_rules.description:
Device-tier rules on the integration's hardware. They bind only actions that fire that
device (and output, when set), so they are not reflected in the integration-wide values
above. Empty on the org preview without `integration_id`.

share_max_duration_seconds.description:
Share-specific TTL cap in seconds. `86400` (1 day) when `share_max_duration` is unset.
Org policy may raise this up to `31536000` (365d). Authoring uses the min of this and
`max_duration_seconds`.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to evaluate curfews, or `"UTC"` when unset.

zone_rules.description:
Organization and integration rules scoped to a zone (`config.zone_id`). They bind only
doors whose effective zone is that zone or below it, so they are not reflected in the
integration-wide values above.

oneOf.description:
Entity-specific metadata (for example integration-specific fields), as string values.
Absent when the entity has none.

name.description: Optional friendly name for the entity.

zone.description: Zone placement: inherit the device's zone, name one explicitly, or none.

Entity.description:
The actual controllable "button" or "sensor".

Examples: Relay 1, Temp Sensor, Light Switch.

data.description: Current `entity_metadata` as a JSON object (best-effort decoded from string values).

schema.description: JSON Schema describing the entity's `entity_metadata` for this provider and entity type.

effective_zone_id.description:
Derived, read-only: the zone the entity is effectively in (`zone` resolved against the
device zone), or null.

oneOf.description: Persisted, entity-specific metadata (integration-specific fields).

entry_kind.description:
Derived, read-only entry kind for switchable entries on Virtual Access devices.
Omitted when the entity is not an entry or the device has no Virtual Access config.

state.description:
Derived, read-only. When local provider config cannot run switchable
open/close/toggle, `{ "status": "invalid", "reason": "<message>" }`.

zone_door_id.description:
Derived, read-only: the door that lists this entity and owns its zone. Present exactly
when `zone_source` is `door`, and also when that door has no zone.

oneOf.description:
Derived, read-only: `entity` when the zone is explicit, `device` when inherited, `door`
when a door that lists this entity owns the zone, null when there is no effective zone.

ExternalReferenceInput.description:
Correlation to a record in an external system of record.

The pair (`source`, `record_id`) is the addressable key: one live invitation per pair per
integration. `revision` is the source's own monotonic version of the record and is the
precondition that keeps a late event from overwriting a newer one.

record_id.description:
Identifier of the record inside that system (reservation, work order, enrolment). Opaque to
OpenApp; up to 128 characters.

revision.description:
Monotonic revision of the external record. When present, OpenApp rejects any later write
carrying a lower revision with `external_revision_stale`.

source.description:
Slug naming the external system, e.g. `mews`, `opera`, `custom-pms`. Lowercase letters,
digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`; up to 64 characters.

ExternalReferenceResponse.description: External correlation as returned by the invitation API.

correlation_id.description: Correlation id of the request that last wrote this reference.

FlaggedResource.description: A resource currently flagged in the lifecycle (shown to admins so they can resolve).

listing_kind.description: The kind written onto every listing this request generates.

GeocodingProviderId.description:
Issuer of a place id. Place ids are opaque to OpenApp and are only interpretable by the provider
that minted them, so every stored or transported place id names its issuer.

GetAccessPortalResponse.description: Response for get access portal by ID (includes integration_id for navigation).

GroupLinkResponse.description: A group's link into an org.

GroupMemberResponse.description:
A member as a requesting org may see them.

Contact details are absent by design: a referencing org may see who can enter its building but
not how to reach them.

GroupProposalResponse.description: One household's proposal state at one org.

pending_members.description: Members waiting for this org to admit them.

GroupResponse.description: A group as returned by the API.

token.description: The one-time token. Returned only by create; redemption never echoes it back.

GroupSiteRef.description: A site a household grants access to.

recurrence.description: Authored recurrence (always `freq: weekly` and an explicit ISO day list).

timezone.description:
IANA timezone for authoring: the spec's zone when recurring, otherwise the org zone
(`UTC` if the org has none). Never the caller's browser zone.

oneOf.description: Provider-derived output/channel selector: the row binds only actions on that output.

zone_id.description:
Zone the row is scoped to (org and integration rows only): it binds only when the acting
effective zone is this zone or a descendant. Must be a live zone of the policy's org.

invitee_name.description:
Name you gave for the invitee. Omitted when none was given, and once the invitation is
accepted or cancelled.

locale.description: Message language the sender chose, or `null` when none was chosen.

sites.description: Sites where this group is linked and the caller is admitted.

PreviewAccessInviteResponse.description:
Effective plan for a create request, produced without persisting anything.

Onboarding an external adapter is the main use: it can check that a desired reservation maps to
portals it is allowed to grant, that the schedule resolves as expected, and which identity
fields organization policy will demand — before any physical access exists.

pending_approval.description: True when creating this invitation would land disabled awaiting admin approval.

required_identity_fields.description:
Identity fields organization policy requires for this invitation: `pin`, `invitee_phone`,
and/or `photo`.

timezone.description: Org IANA timezone used to evaluate invitation curfews.

unlinked_portal_ids.description:
Portals that would be granted but do not currently resolve to a live door device, so the
guest link would not open them.

valid.description:
Always true on a 200. A request that would be rejected returns the same status, error code,
and message that create would return.

type's default principals.

effective zone is this zone or a descendant. Must be a live zone of the policy's org.

integration_id.description: The site (integration) to propose the household to.

ProviderType.description: Integration provider type (e.g. homeassistant, knx, mqtt).

degradation.description: Present when an over-capacity org slowed this open; clients show a readable warning.

uses_remaining.description: Uses left after this execution; omitted when the invitation has no use limit.

door_image_thumb_url.description:
Presigned URL for the `thumb` rendition of the door image, for avatar-sized
renders. Absent when the source is already thumb-sized; fall back to
`door_image_url`.

door_image_url.description: Presigned URL for door image (loaded asynchronously as card background).

entry_kind.description:
Entry type configured on the linked portal device (`entry_kind` in its
`virtual_access` metadata). Default `door`.

has_lights.description: Whether the portal has light devices configured (controls light button visibility).

oneOf.description: Effective door hold when any opener is held (guest-visible).

label.description: Localized portal name: string or object { "en": "...", "he": "..." }.

oneOf.description:
Enforced integration-scoped minimum interval between `switchable.open` calls.
A second open inside the interval returns 429 `provider_open_rate_limited`.

openable.description:
Whether the portal is linked to a live door device (i.e. can actually be opened).
When false, the invite UI disables the open action (a misconfigured/unlinked portal).

wifi_available.description:
The door's zone is covered by a Wi-Fi network the guest may join, for example
where the door has no cellular signal. A suggestion only: the door opens either way.
The networks are in `wifi_networks` on the response.
The acted-on device's zone is covered by a Wi-Fi network (see `PortalOpen`).

locale.description:
Locale code (`en`, `he`, `pt_br`) of the language the invitation's messages are sent in
for this link's contact.

channel.description: `sms` (default) or `email`. The destination is the matching contact on the invitation.

oneOf.description: Access-control integration summary (building name, address, photo).

audience.description: Whether anyone holding the link may use the invitation, or only the named contacts.

building.description:
Building (integration) summary: `name` (LocalizedString) and optional `location` fields
from integration config (`formatted_address`, `city`, `country`).

contact_challenge_required.description:
True when the bearer must prove they are one of the named contacts before the invitation
can be used. Which contact was matched is never echoed back, so this cannot be used to
enumerate who an invitation is for.

contact_display_name.description: The display name of the contact this token resolved to, when it resolved to one.

curfew_windows.description: Effective forbidden hour windows for invitation access (informational).

oneOf.description:
Event location (address / map-picked coordinates) owned by this invite, distinct from the
building/portal location surfaced via `access_control`.

invite_url.description: Guest-facing invite URL (shareable link for SMS/email).

location_mode.description:
How the invite resolves its event location: `none` (hide all location, including the
building address), `explicit` (own location), or `inherit` (building location). Lets the
guest UI suppress the building address when the invite opts out of location entirely.

max_uses.description: Total uses allowed; omitted when the invitation has no use limit.

name.description: Optional admin-defined label (management UI "name"); exposed for link previews and guests who already know the invite by name.

photo_url.description: Presigned URL for the invite's main photo (best-effort).

renewal_requested.description: True when the authenticated requester already submitted a pending renewal request.

timezone.description: Org IANA timezone used to evaluate invitation curfews (`UTC` when unset).

uses_remaining.description: Uses left before the limit is consumed; omitted when the invitation has no use limit.

wifi_networks.description:
Wi-Fi networks that cover the invitation's doors, with credentials, ordered by priority.
Present only for an active invitation whose grants are shown, and only when at least one
grant has `wifi_available`. Never part of a link preview.

guest_id.description:
Stable per-device guest fingerprint (ULID). Either the one supplied by the client (cookie
or `X-Guest-Id`) or a freshly minted one. Echoed so native clients can persist it and send
it back via `X-Guest-Id` on subsequent public-access calls. Used only for audit
attribution — it confers no access.

invite_id.description:
ULID of the invite (= value of the `oa_access_invite` cookie). Echoed
in the body so non-browser clients can construct the cookie without
relying on a platform cookie jar for `HttpOnly` `Set-Cookie` responses.

PublicInviteWifiNetwork.description: A Wi-Fi network as the invite page shows it.

credentials_unavailable.description:
The credentials could not be read right now. The network is listed so the guest knows it
exists and can ask the host; the door itself opens without Wi-Fi.

hidden.description: The network does not broadcast its SSID.

notes.description: Where the network reaches, for example "lobby only".

password.description: Passphrase (`wpa_psk`) or enterprise password. Absent for open networks.

image_thumb_url.description:
Presigned URL for the `thumb` rendition of the same photo, for small renders.
Absent when the source is already thumb-sized; fall back to `image_url`.

image_url.description: Presigned URL for the integration or location photo.

message.description: Admin-authored text for `disabled`, as localized JSON.

provider_place_id.description:
Opaque place id for the address, when it was resolved by a maps provider, together with the
provider that issued it. Clients that recognize the provider can link to the place itself
(e.g. Google Maps URLs `query_place_id`) instead of a bare coordinate; the rest fall back to
the address text. Both fields are present together or not at all.

status.description:
Directory status when this summary describes the visitor directory: one of `ready`,
`empty`, `not_configured`, `disabled`. Absent for the access-control summary.

PublicPortalCreateSessionRequest.description: Start a visitor session with a directory entry.

mode.description: `voice`, `video` or `message` (case-insensitive); any other value is rejected with 400.

target_entity_id.description: ID of the directory entry (listing entity) to contact. Required; 400 when blank.

callees_notified.description: True when at least one callee had a push subscription so notification was sent (or attempted).

min_interval_ms.description: Enforced minimum milliseconds between `switchable.open` calls on this integration.

reason.description:
Why the door is not reachable, when the server knows. `door_not_connected`: the portal has
no door (it was purged, or never linked), so retrying cannot help. Omitted when reachable
and when the cause is a door that exists but did not answer.

oneOf.description: Access-control integration summary (building name, address, photo).
Visitor directory device summary for this portal (building directory name, photo).

door_connected.description:
False when the portal has no door to open: the door was purged, or the portal was never
linked to one. The printed QR code stays valid; an admin can link a door again.

door_image_url.description: Image URL for the door (presigned S3 URL from media service).

entry_kind.description:
Entry type configured on the linked portal device (`entry_kind` in its
`virtual_access` metadata). Default `door`.

oneOf.description: Effective door hold when any opener is held (guest-visible).

call_available.description: True when at least one resident (receives_calls) exists. When false, voice/video are excluded from allowed_actions.

denial_reasons.description:
Why this entry cannot be called; empty when nothing blocks a call. `no_callees`: nobody
at this entry receives calls. `dnd`: Do Not Disturb is on for this entry, or no callee
can currently be notified. `guest_disabled`: visitor access to this entry is turned off
by policy.

effective_display_name.description: Server-resolved visitor name. Clients render this and do not recompute it.

location_detail.description: Unit/floor subtitle as a `LocalizedString`. Absent when it adds nothing beyond the title.

floor_order.description: Building `floor_order` from virtual_access integration config (canonical keys).

message.description:
Admin-authored text shown to visitors when `status` is `disabled`. Omitted for every
other status.

status.description:
One of `ready`, `empty`, `not_configured`, `disabled`. Each carries its own visitor
copy, so a building with no occupants reads differently from an intercom that was never
set up.

call_target_display_name.description: Localized listing / unit title for call UI (caller/callee).

call_target_location_line.description: Single line for listing + floor (e.g. "3 · Floor 2").

callees_notified.description: Whether at least one callee received a push notification. Caller uses this to skip peer-unavailable retries when false.

has_lights.description: Whether the portal has light devices configured. Callee-only.

mode.description:
Session mode: `voice`, `video` or `message`. Video is on by default when the mode is
`video`.

device_ids.description:
IDs of the camera devices configured on the session's portal (cameras outside the
portal's organization are excluded). Empty when the session has no portal device. Stream
URLs are not included.

applies_to.description:
Principal kinds the row binds; unknown and empty values are rejected. Omitted binds the
type's default principals.

end.description: Inclusive local end of the window, in `HH:MM`; a later end wraps midnight.

start.description: Inclusive local start of the window, in `HH:MM`.

QuotaKey.description:
A metered resource. Lifetime keys count resources that currently exist; temporal keys count
usage within a period.

QuotaPeriod.description:
Window kind for a quota. `Lifetime` is "ever / right now"; `Day`/`Week`/`Month`
reset on calendar boundaries (UTC); `PerSession` resets per opaque session id.

QuotaReport.description: Full quota usage report for an org.

oneOf.description:
Over-capacity remediation snapshot. Present only when the degradation system is
enabled and the caller is permitted to see it; `null` otherwise.

QuotaUnit.description:
Machine-readable unit for a quota quantity. `Count` is a plain integer of the
key's noun (door opens, devices, …); `Seconds` is a duration clients may render
in larger units (e.g. minutes for video chat).

QuotaUsage.description: Single (key, period) entry in a usage report.

external_ref.description:
The external record this reconcile is about. It identifies the invitation, so the caller
does not need to track OpenApp invitation ids.

oneOf.description:
Desired invitation. Required when `state` is `active`, ignored when `revoked`. It must not
carry its own `external_ref`: the top-level reference owns the binding.

state.description: Desired state for that record. Defaults to `active`.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this body is a replay of an earlier reconcile carrying the same
`Idempotency-Key`; nothing was written by this request.

oneOf.description: Invitation state after reconciling.

invite_link_id.description:
The invitation serving the external record. Absent only when the desired state is `revoked`
and no invitation exists for the record.

invite_token.description:
Guest bearer token, returned **once**, only by the call that created the invitation. A
replayed reconcile omits it; use `regenerate-token` to obtain a fresh link.

invite_url.description: Guest-facing invite URL, with the same one-time visibility as `invite_token`.

ReconcileInviteState.description: Desired lifecycle state of the invitation that serves an external record.

accept_on_signed_in_account.description:
Attach the invitation to the signed-in account when its mailbox is not the invited email.
The invited address is not stored. Required only in that case; omitted otherwise.

merge_accounts.description:
Start a combine-accounts offer when the invited email or phone already belongs to someone else.
The invitation stays pending until that offer is confirmed and redeem is called again.

phone_action.description:
`keep` leaves the account's phone unchanged. `replace` saves the invited number over it.
Required when the account already has a different phone and the invited number is free.

accepted.description:
False when `merge` was created and the invitation is still pending.
Omitted when the invitation was accepted, so older clients treat a missing field as accepted.

invite_url.description: Guest-facing invite URL (shareable link for SMS/email).

applies_to.description:
Principal kinds the row binds; unknown and empty values are rejected. Omitted binds the
type's default principals.

resource_selector.description:
Entities requiring confirmation: `"*"`, one entity ULID, or a non-empty array of entity
ULIDs. Omitted applies to every entity.

sms_consent_confirmed.description:
Must be `true` when the invitation has a phone: confirms the person you invite agreed to
receive text messages from OpenApp at that number. Not needed for email-only
invitations; send `{}`.

Must be `true` when the invitation has a phone: confirms the person being invited agreed
to receive text messages from OpenApp at that number. Not needed for email-only
invitations; send `{}`.

ResourceImageUrlResponse.description:
Resource-scoped image URL response (does not expose asset_id).
When no image is uploaded, returns 204 No Content (not 404).

ResourceLifecycle.description:
Lifecycle timestamps of a resource (created, updated, soft-deleted, scheduled purge and hard
delete), at the top level of the resource object. Timestamps that are not set are omitted.

ResourceState.description: Degradation state of a single resource.

Role.description: A role name (e.g. admin, users:read) assigned to a user in an org.

ScriptingExecutionSummary.description:
A scripting execution as returned by list endpoints: every field of a scripting execution
except `result`. Fetch the execution by id to read its result.

SelectionPolicy.description: How excess resources are chosen when the admin has not pinned survivors via `quota_keep`.

default_locale.description:
Supported locale code (`en`, `zh_cn`, `es`, `ru`, `pt_br`, `de`, `fr`, `ja`,
`ar`, `it`, `he`), or `null` to clear.

timezone.description: IANA timezone. Empty or null clears to UTC fallback.

zone_ids.description:
The complete set of zones the network covers. Each must be a live zone of the network's
org.

SingleResourceOutputOptionsQuery.description:
Query parameters for single-resource operations (get/create/update/delete/restore).
Omits `only_deleted` since it only applies to list endpoints.

SiteAccessDevice.description: One device in one section. A device may appear in more than one section.

deleted.description: True when the device is soft-deleted but still referenced by a door.

doors.description: Doors this device serves in this role (union of `entities[].doors`).

entities.description: Entities on this device playing this section's role. Empty for cameras.

integration_id.description: Owning integration — usually not the site's own integration.

SiteAccessDeviceDoor.description: A door (portal device) a device serves.

auto_off_config.description: The door's `auto_off_config` for this light entry. Lights only.

oneOf.description: The door's life-safety class and attestation, for open gating.

SiteAccessDeviceEntity.description: An entity on the device that plays the section's role.

doors.description: Doors this entity serves, each carrying that door's light auto-off config.

label.description: The label the door gave this opener/light, when set.

SiteAccessDeviceRole.description: Which door-side list put a device in a section.

unresolved.description: Door references that resolve to no device. Never empty-by-omission.

SiteAccessDoorLifeSafety.description:
A door's life-safety class and commissioning attestation, as stored on the door.

The server refuses `switchable.open` and `switchable.toggle` on an opening that has no class,
or whose class requires an attestation that is missing or incomplete (409
`life_safety_class_required` / `life_safety_attestation_required`). This object reports the
stored values so clients can show whether the door can be opened.

SiteAccessUnresolvedReason.description: Why a door's reference has no device to show.

SiteAccessUnresolvedRef.description: A door reference with nothing to show.

reference.description: The raw id from the door's metadata (entity id for openers/lights, device id for cameras).

SiteAccessWifiCover.description: A zone of the site that a network reaches, and whether it reaches it directly.

via_zone_id.description:
The ancestor zone the network is linked to. Absent when the network is linked to
`zone_id` itself.

oneOf.description: Name of `via_zone_id`.

zone_id.description: A site zone (one that holds doors) the network applies to.

SiteAccessWifiNetwork.description: A Wi-Fi network that applies to at least one door of the site.

covers.description: The site zones this network applies to, and how.

has_credentials.description: False for `open` networks. Credentials are never part of this response.

SiteAccessZone.description: A zone that holds at least one door of the site.

doors.description: Doors of the site placed in this zone.

path.description: Zone names from the root zone down to this zone, inclusive.

doors_without_zone.description: Doors with no zone. Their invitations offer no Wi-Fi and no zone policy binds them.

wifi_networks.description: Networks that apply to the site's doors. Omitted when the requester lacks `zones:read`.

zones.description: Zones that hold the site's doors. Omitted when the requester lacks `zones:read`.

role.description: Site role (`admin`, `resident`, `technician`) or, for a via-group row, the group role.

source.description: `org_member` or `via_group`. Via-group rows have no site role to edit.

oneOf.description: When set, changes whether anyone holding the link may use the invitation.

contacts.description: When set, replaces the invitation's contacts. Omitted leaves them unchanged.

creation_justification.description: Why this invitation was created (required when `invitation_require_justification` applies).

curfew_exempt.description: Admin-only emergency exception: skip invitation curfew at redemption.

oneOf.description:
External-record precondition and correlation. When present, `source`/`record_id` must match
the invitation's stored reference (or bind it for the first time), and a `revision` older
than the stored one is rejected with `external_revision_stale` so a late event cannot
restore an earlier room, window, or portal set.

location_id.description:
Only consumed when `location_mode` is `explicit`: the reusable org location id to bind.
When the mode is `explicit` and this is absent, the existing bound location is kept.

oneOf.description:
When set, replaces the event-location mode (`none`, `explicit`, or `inherit`). Absent
leaves the mode and location unchanged.

max_devices.description: Virtual keycard limit: max unique devices allowed. JSON `null` means unlimited.

pin.description: Omitted leaves the stored PIN unchanged; JSON `null` clears it.

portal_ids.description: When set, replaces portal grants. Array order is the display order on the public invite page.

schedules.description:
When set, replaces all schedule entries. This is the only way to change validity or
recurrence.

device_id.description: Door device id. Must be a virtual_access_portal device in this integration. Use null to unlink.

directory_id.description: Directory device id. Must be a virtual_access_directory device in this integration. Use null to unlink.

expires_at.description: [RFC 3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339) absolute expiration timestamp (UTC). Mutually exclusive with `expires_in`. Optional; if omitted, expiry is unchanged.

expires_in.description: Duration per [RFC 5545 §3.3.6](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545#section-3.3.6) (ISO 8601 `P1D`, `PT1H`, …; no months/years) or compact tokens `s`/`m`/`h`/`d`/`w` (`M` is minutes). Max 3650d (10 years). `1y` is rejected. Mutually exclusive with `expires_at`. Optional; if omitted, expiry is unchanged.

zone_id.description: Omit for no change, `null` to clear, or a zone id (same org) to place the device.

metadata.description:
Update (replace) persisted entity metadata.

- omitted: no change
- `null`: clear metadata
- object: replace with the provided map

name.description:
Update entity name.

- omitted: no change
- `null`: clear
- string: set (trimmed; an empty string clears)

oneOf.description: Replace the zone placement. Omit for no change.

admission_mode.description:
approve waits for each member to be admitted; auto admits them immediately; pinned holds a
fixed member set until an explicit re-sync.

resync.description: With pinned mode, re-reads the group's current membership and admits the difference.

config.description:
Tri-state patch semantics for `config`:
- field omitted: do not change config
- `"config": null`: clear config (set to None)
- `"config": { ... }`: replace config (do not merge), except write-only credential
  fields (schema `format: password`): omitted keeps the stored value, `null` clears it

oneOf.description:
Human-friendly name for this integration.
Accepts string or LocalizedString map, e.g. { "en": "Name", "he": "שם" }.

secrets.description:
Tri-state patch semantics for `secrets` (stored in Secrets Manager):
- field omitted: do not change secrets
- `"secrets": null`: clear secrets
- `"secrets": { ... }`: replace secrets

UpdateInvitationRequest.description: Fields of a pending invitation that can be edited. Omit a field to leave it unchanged.

date_of_birth.description:
Replaces the parent-declared date of birth (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Must classify as under 16.
Send an empty string to clear it. Omit to leave it unchanged.

default_roles.description: Replaces the roles assigned on accept (within the inviting org).

locale.description:
Replaces the message language: a supported locale code. Applies to messages sent from now
on; a message already sent keeps the language it was written in.

oneOf.description: Replaces the site (and listing) access applied when the invitation is redeemed.

parent_id.description:
Move the org under a new parent (re-parent). When present and different from the current
parent, the org (and its whole subtree) is moved under `parent_id`. Requires `admin` on the
destination parent (or an ancestor) in addition to `update_orgs` on the org being moved.

config.description: Omitted preserves the current config. Explicit JSON `null` is rejected with 400.

phone.description:
E.164 phone. Send `null` to clear; omit field to leave unchanged. When set,
`phone_verified_at` is stamped server-side (admin-attested verification).

oneOf.description:
Omit to keep the stored credentials, which is only allowed while `security` is unchanged.
Changing `security` to a type that needs credentials requires them here.

parent_zone_id.description: Omit for no change, `null` to make the zone a root, or a zone id to reparent.

site_ids.description: Replace Access-site memberships. Omit for no change. Empty clears all (unbind).

UsageActor.description:
The actor behind a usage entry. Registered users and guests are kept in disjoint fields so the
(spoofable) guest fingerprint is never confused with a trusted user identity by the client.

guest_id.description: Per-device guest fingerprint. Present only when `kind == "guest"`.

user_id.description: Trusted registered-user id. Present only when `kind == "user"`.

email.description: Email address (used for login and provisioning). May be an internal placeholder when no verified email is available.

merged_into_user_id.description:
When set, this user was merged into the user with this id; use that user as the live
identity.

User.description: A provisioned user (identity) in the system.

date_of_birth.description:
Parent-declared date of birth (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Present only while the invitation is pending.
Applied to the account at redeem when the account has none.

default_group_ids.description: Groups joined when the invitation is redeemed, in the same transaction as the org role.

invitee_name.description: Name the inviter gave for the invitee. Present only while the invitation is pending.

locale.description: Message language the sender chose, or `null` when none was chosen.

message_locale.description:
Shipped locale code of the language the invitation messages are written in: the invitee's
own account language, else `locale`, else the org default, else English. Present only while
the invitation is pending.

phone.description: SMS recipient when the invite includes a phone (E.164).

phone_transport.description: `sms` or `whatsapp` when a phone PIN was sent.

resend_available_at.description:
When a resend is next accepted (RFC 3339). Present only while the invitation is pending;
a resend before this time is refused with 429.

email_is_synthetic.description: True when `email` is an internal placeholder (phone-only account or identity-provider merge claimant) and must not be shown as a mailbox.

WifiCredentials.description: Secret part of a Wi-Fi network. Stored in Secrets Manager, never in Postgres.

password.description: Passphrase (`wpa_psk`) or enterprise password (`wpa_enterprise`). Absent for `open`.

WifiNetwork.description: A Wi-Fi network owned by an org.

hidden.description: The network does not broadcast its SSID.

zone_ids.description: Zones this network covers. Invitations to doors in these zones offer the network.

WifiNetworkResponse.description:
A Wi-Fi network as returned by the API. Credentials are never included; use the
credentials endpoint.

Zone.description:
A physical space owned by an org (recursive for hierarchy).

Example: Floor 1 > Living Room > TV Nook. Placement of devices and entities is never
constrained by vendor: any device or entity of the same org may be placed in any zone.

ZonePlacement.description:
How an entity is placed in a zone.

`inherit` follows the device's zone, `explicit` names a zone, and `none` keeps the entity out
of every zone even when its device has one. Sent as `{"mode":"inherit"}`,
`{"mode":"explicit","zone_id":"…"}`, or `{"mode":"none"}`.

ZoneProviderLinkResponse.description: Provider provenance as exposed on zone responses (the zone id is implied).

site_ids.description:
Access sites (`virtual_access` integrations) this zone is a member of, sorted.
Empty means unbound (Resources-only until bound; never offered on Access pickers).

ZoneRuleResponse.description: One organization- or integration-tier policy scoped to a zone.

zone_path.description: Zone names from the root to this zone (inclusive).

ZoneSource.description: Where an entity's effective zone came from.

path.description: Ancestors root first, including the zone itself.

devices_placed.description: Devices whose zone this sync changed.

entities_placed.description: Entities whose placement this sync changed.

skipped_manual.description:
Devices and entities left alone because a user changed their placement since the last
sync, or because a door lists the entity and owns its zone.

zones_created.description: Org zones created for provider zones with no unique name match.

zones_linked.description: Provider zones newly linked to an existing org zone (by unique normalized name).

device_count.description: Devices placed directly in this zone.

entity_count.description: Entities whose effective zone is this zone (not descendants).

api_key.name: X-API-Key
api_key.description: OpenApp API key issued via `POST /api-keys`, sent verbatim as `X-API-Key: {origin}_openapp_{secret}`. `{origin}` is the deployment origin the key was issued by; the API root is `{origin}/api/v1`, which the SDKs derive from the key. Do not send API keys in `Authorization`: the gateway reserves it for JWTs and rejects an API key there with 401.
